agricultural: Agricultural land shows large, contiguous parcels with uniform texture and regular geometric field boundaries. It differs from golf course by lacking manicured fairways and sand traps; from storage tanks by having no circular metallic structures; and from chaparral by being less dense and more regularly patterned than shrubland.
airplane: Airplanes appear as elongated metallic objects with distinct fuselage, wings, and tail, parked on hardstand areas adjacent to runways. They are easily distinguished from runway by being discrete movable objects rather than linear pavement; overpass appears as elevated road structure rather than aircraft; agricultural fields lack any metallic aircraft shapes.
baseballdiamond: Baseball diamonds are characterized by their distinctive diamond-shaped infield with raised pitcher's mound, outfield grass, and surrounding dirt. They differ from tennis courts by having diamond geometry rather than rectangular with net; parking lots have no organized sports field markings; harbors contain water and docks rather than sports infrastructure.
beach: Beaches appear as narrow, light-toned sandy strips along water bodies, often with visible wave patterns and shoreline curvature. They contrast with harbors by having no man-made docks or breakwaters; chaparral appears as darker, vegetated hillsides rather than sandy shorelines; agricultural fields show no coastal sand deposits.
buildings: Buildings are characterized by rectangular footprints with visible roofs, shadows, and regular spatial arrangements in urban blocks. They differ from dense residential by being commercial structures rather than housing units with yards; parking lots are adjacent open spaces with vehicles rather than roofed structures; mobile home parks contain smaller, elongated trailer units.
chaparral: Chaparral appears as dense, low, dark-green shrub vegetation with irregular edges covering hillsides, showing rough texture. It contrasts with agricultural land by lacking field boundaries and uniform crop rows; beach has no vegetation cover; golf course features mowed fairways and bunkers rather than wild scrub.
denseresidential: Dense residential areas show small housing units packed closely together with narrow streets, tiny yards, and uniform block patterns. They differ from mobile home parks by having permanent foundations rather than trailer units; buildings are larger commercial structures rather than houses; sparse residential has larger lots and more vegetation between units.
forest: Forests appear as extensive areas with dense, tall tree cover, dark green canopy with rough, uneven texture and no visible ground. They contrast with dense residential by lacking any buildings or street networks; freeway is linear paved corridor cutting through landscape; agricultural land has regular crop patterns rather than natural tree cover.
freeway: Freeways are wide linear strips of paved concrete with multiple lanes, clear lane markings, and overpass intersections. They differ from overpass by being ground-level continuous pavement rather than elevated bridge structures; runway is shorter and lacks lane divisions; storage tanks are discrete circular objects rather than linear transportation corridors.
golfcourse: Golf courses are large green areas with mowed fairways, lighter roughs, sand bunkers, and small water hazards, arranged in a connected network. They contrast with agricultural fields by having scattered bunkers and water features rather than uniform crop rows; chaparral appears as wild, dense scrub; storage tanks are metallic circular structures.
harbor: Harbors show calm water areas enclosed by docks, piers, ships, and cranes, with visible boundaries and artificial shoreline modifications. They differ from parking lots by containing water and vessels rather than vehicles; storage tanks appear as circular metallic containers inland; beach lacks dock infrastructure and ships.
intersection: Intersections show cross-shaped road junctions with clear pavement markings, turn lanes, and traffic islands. They contrast with dense residential by being road features rather than housing blocks; river appears as natural water feature; freeway is a continuous corridor rather than a local junction.
mediumresidential: Medium residential consists of moderate-sized houses on medium lots with regular spacing, tree-lined streets, and observable driveways. It differs from dense residential by having larger yards and more space between units; mobile home parks show narrower trailers rather than houses; buildings are larger commercial structures.
mobilehomepark: Mobile home parks show rows of small, narrow rectangular trailer units arranged in dense, uniform clusters with narrow access roads. They contrast with dense residential by having no permanent foundations or varied house designs; buildings are taller commercial structures; tennis courts show net and court markings.
overpass: Overpasses are elevated road segments supported by pillars, crossing above other roads or terrain, with visible ramps and shadows. They differ from freeway by being raised structures rather than ground-level pavement; runway lacks pillars and elevation; chaparral shows no elevated transportation structures.
parkinglot: Parking lots are flat, open areas with visible rows of parked vehicles in organized lanes with painted markings. They contrast with harbors by having vehicles rather than ships and water; buildings are roofed structures rather than open lots; baseball diamonds show sports field markings rather than parking rows.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, linear, dark water bodies with sinuous curves and riparian vegetation along banks. They differ from intersections by being natural water features rather than road junctions; agricultural fields show no water channel; freeway is paved transport corridor.
runway: Runways are long, straight, wide paved strips with clear parallel markings, end zones, and no intersecting cross streets. They contrast with airplane by being pavement infrastructure rather than discrete aircraft objects; freeway is narrower with lane markings and curves; overpass crosses above other roads rather than being surface pavement.
sparseresidential: Sparse residential shows widely spaced houses surrounded by large vegetated lots, with visible driveways and sparse road networks. It differs from dense residential by having much larger lots and more vegetation; mobile home parks have clustered trailers; chaparral shows no houses or lawns.
storagetanks: Storage tanks appear as large circular metallic structures with domed or flat roofs, arranged in clusters, with visible shadows and connecting pipes. They contrast with agricultural fields by having industrial structures rather than crops; freeway is linear pavement; golf course shows no circular metallic containers.
tenniscourt: Tennis courts are rectangular playing areas with visible nets, court lines, and smooth surfaces, often with surrounding fences. They differ from dense residential by being sports courts rather than housing units; baseball diamonds are diamond-shaped rather than rectangular; buildings are roofed structures rather than open courts.
